name: Peulletai
title: Levitical gatekeeper in the temple
summary: Peulletai was one of the sons of Obed-Edom, a Levite who served as a gatekeeper at God's temple in Jerusalem during King David's reign. He was part of a large family blessed by God, and his father Obed-Edom is known for having the Lord's ark kept in his house. Peulletai is mentioned in connection with the organization of temple service.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned among the sons of Obed-Edom
keyEvents.description: Peulletai is listed as the eighth son of Obed-Edom in the register of Levitical gatekeepers organized during David's reign.

keyEvents.title: Obed-Edom's Family Blessed by God
keyEvents.description: The Bible tells us that God blessed Obed-Edom and all his household, resulting in many sons and descendants, including Peulletai.

keyEvents.title: Organization of Gatekeeping Service
keyEvents.description: David organized the Levites into divisions for temple service, and Obed-Edom's sons, including Peulletai, were assigned gatekeeping duties at the storehouses on the south side.

keyEvents.title: The Lord's Ark in Obed-Edom's House
keyEvents.description: Before Peulletai's time, the Lord's ark had been kept in Obed-Edom's house for three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-Edom and all his household during that period.
